project.name: Titan AI
project.description: Autonomous software engineering operating system, implemented as Titan Core: seven cooperating engines (Planner, Orchestrator, Context, Knowledge, Execution, Validation, Learning). See architecture.md Section 7 and decisions.md ADR-0002.

next_phase.name: Production Release
next_phase.blocked_reason: Awaiting Phase 015 completion, which is itself governance-blocked pending a hosting/deployment-target decision (tech_stack.md §2/§5) and resolution or risk-acceptance (via ADR) of existing high/critical dependency vulnerabilities (deployment_strategy.md §7).

tech_stack.notes: Selected TypeScript with Node.js, npm workspaces, Vitest, ESLint, and Prettier for the initial Titan AI monorepo scaffold (see tech_stack.md and ADR-0003).

architecture.notes: architecture.md Section 7 defines the approved Titan Core engine architecture (7 engines), with security architecture governance established in Section 6.

engines.name: Planner Engine
engines.notes: createPlan, validatePlan, optimizePlan, estimatePlan, and explainPlan are implemented (Milestones 1-6). cancelPlan remains a NotImplementedError stub; not required by any Phase 008 exit criterion.

engines.name: Orchestrator Engine
engines.notes: orchestrate, executeWorkflow, getWorkflowStatus, pauseWorkflow, resumeWorkflow, cancelWorkflow, and dispatchWorkflow are all implemented (Milestones 1-7). All seven public API methods are implemented with no remaining NotImplementedError stubs. Dispatch and escalation are structural only; no scheduling, execution, retries, or cross-engine runtime calls.

engines.name: Context Engine
engines.notes: Phase 013 Milestone 1 added ContextEngine, extending BaseEngine and implementing the shared lifecycle contract (initialize/start/stop/health/metadata/version/contractVersion/getState) via specification/engine_api.md §3.1; composes the pre-existing ContextManager unchanged; declares capabilities: [] since no repository document names a Context Engine business method.

engines.name: Execution Engine
engines.notes: execute, getExecutionStatus, and reportResult are implemented (Milestones 1-5: runtime foundation, complete planned domain model, ExecutionBuilder/execute() - deterministic structural translation of an Orchestrator WorkflowDispatchResult into an ExecutionRecord, ExecutionValidator/getExecutionStatus() - deterministic structural validation of an ExecutionRecord, and ExecutionStatusTracker/reportResult() - deterministic structural summarization of an ExecutionRecord; despite its name, reportResult() performs no real result reporting). cancelExecution remains an unimplemented NotImplementedError stub; a dedicated governance review (see phases/phase-010-execution-engine-implementation.md) confirmed this is not required by any Phase 010 exit criterion, since the 'dispatch-to-result lifecycle' phrase used in the exit criteria is never defined anywhere in the repository.

engines.name: Validation Engine
engines.notes: validate and getValidationStatus are implemented (Milestones 1-5: runtime foundation, complete planned domain model, ValidationBuilder/validate() - deterministic structural translation of an Execution Engine ExecutionSummary/ExecutionRecord into a ValidationPipelineResult, ValidationValidator/getValidationStatus() - deterministic structural validation of a ValidationVerdict, and ValidationEvidenceCollector/ValidationPipelineRunner - deterministic structural evidence collection composed with verdict construction, wired into validate()). approveValidation and rejectValidation remain unimplemented NotImplementedError stubs; a dedicated specification audit and governance review (see phases/phase-011-validation-engine-implementation.md) confirmed neither is required by any Phase 011 exit criterion or specification/engine_api.md requirement, and that implementing them would require either persistence (a validation store/lookup mechanism) or business logic (approval authority/audit semantics), both out of scope for deterministic structural processing.

engines.name: Learning Engine
engines.notes: observeCycle, generateProposal, prepareKnowledgeHandoff, and analyzeCycle are implemented (Milestones 1-6: runtime foundation, complete domain model, LearningObservationBuilder/observeCycle(), LearningProposalBuilder/generateProposal(), LearningKnowledgeHandoffBuilder/prepareKnowledgeHandoff(), and LearningLessonBuilder/LearningFlaggedRiskBuilder/LearningProposedAdrBuilder/LearningPipelineBuilder/analyzeCycle()). All four public API methods are implemented with no remaining NotImplementedError stubs. A dedicated Governance Resolution (see phases/phase-012-learning-engine-implementation.md) determined that actual Knowledge Engine-side consumption of Learning Engine handoff artifacts is architecturally assigned to the Knowledge Engine and to Phase 013's cross-engine validation scope, not to Phase 012; it remains unimplemented and unscoped pending Phase 013 or a future ADR.

titan_core.notes: Implementation order follows the Titan Core architecture data-flow dependency order: Context first, then the shared framework, then security governance, then Knowledge, Planner, Orchestrator, Execution, Validation, and Learning. Phase 013 (Titan Core Integration and Hardening) is complete: all seven engines are wired into apps/titan-shell via the shared EngineRegistry, end-to-end and cross-engine-boundary integration tests exist (tests/integration/), and a security/performance hardening review is recorded at .titan/reviews/2026-07-31-phase-013-security-performance-hardening.md. Phase 014 (Test Coverage Completion) is complete: coverage reporting infrastructure (npm run coverage), Knowledge Engine/LifecycleManager/ContextManager coverage gap closures, and a CI quality-gate workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml) were added, with three unresolved items carried forward (npm audit findings not yet remediated/risk-accepted, unenforced coverage thresholds pending a domain/application folder-mapping decision, and a confirmed reproducible flaky test in tests/unit/validation-engine.test.ts). No engine's business logic changed during Phase 013 or Phase 014. Phase 015 (Deployment Readiness) is in-progress, not complete: three CI-gate milestones (format-check, no-skipped-tests, basic secrets pattern scan) were added to .github/workflows/ci.yml and verified, but every remaining milestone (artifact packaging, staging environment, staging validation, production deployment, rollback) is governance-blocked — no hosting/deployment target has been selected (tech_stack.md §5) and production deployment is additionally blocked by unresolved high/critical dependency vulnerabilities with no risk-acceptance ADR (deployment_strategy.md §7). No deployment infrastructure was invented to work around this.

quality.notes: test_coverage_percent is the overall statement/line coverage reported by npm run coverage (Vitest v8 provider) as of Phase 014 closure; no per-tier (domain/application) threshold is enforced (see phases/phase-014-test-coverage-completion.md Review/Findings). known_open_test_issues counts the confirmed, reproducible flaky test in tests/unit/validation-engine.test.ts ('never reads policyRules or governanceRules'), tracked as a Phase 014 follow-up, not resolved. known_open_security_issues (8 = 3 moderate + 3 high + 2 critical) reflects the npm audit findings from Phase 013's hardening review (devDependency transitives introduced when @vitest/coverage-v8 was installed); none remediated or risk-accepted via an ADR per security_policy.md §8. The 5 high/critical of these are the specific subset blocking production deployment per deployment_strategy.md §7.
